clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog: 10 U.S.C. 1035 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121) prints the order as current text with no ending statement; 10 U.S.C. 1035(b), whose held text lets the President prescribe an interest rate not exceeding 10 percent a year, remains in force; no held later instrument supersedes the prescribed rate.
clauses.reason: The paragraph prescribes interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, on amounts deposited under 10 U.S.C. 1035, effective September 1, 1966. It has no own-terms end and no held instrument changes the rate. 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) still authorizes a presidentially prescribed rate not above 10 percent, and the U.S. Code prints the order as current text, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11298 of August 14, 1966 (31 FR 10915), Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, prescribes under section 1035 of title 10, U.S. Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services under that section accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, effective September 1, 1966. The packet text is bounded to the target clause envelope because the heading was not segmented, but the held Federal Register page text (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11298.txt) carries the heading Executive Order 11298, Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, directly above the paragraph, and the order has no other paragraph. Search of held texts for the number EO 11298 finds only the order and the 1989 OFR codification; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends it. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. 1035 note prints the order as current text. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) still provides that interest at a rate prescribed by the President, not to exceed 10 percent a year, accrues on amounts deposited, so the statute the order implements remains in force and the prescribed rate equals its ceiling. The sentence on September 1, 1966 is a start date, not an end. The term-signal records attached to the packet for this order come from the statute's notes (Pub. L. 89-538 and Pub. L. 90-122) and concern deposits and payments, not the rate prescribed by this order. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.
